title: Why C

dx.label: THE DIAGNOSIS
dx.name: Venous CO2 (gas) embolism
dx.text: Insufflated CO2 entered a vein. The gas is now in the right heart, blocking blood flow to the lungs.

items: **Stop insufflation, release the pneumoperitoneum.** No more gas enters the vein.
**100% oxygen, hyperventilate.** Treats the hypoxemia and clears CO2 faster.
**Head-down, left side down (Durant).** Keeps gas away from the right ventricular outflow tract.
**Aspirate a central line if one is already in.** It pulls gas out of the right heart. Support the circulation. CPR if arrest.
! **Not a vagal reflex:** that causes bradycardia. The sudden EtCO2 fall is dead space, so don't cut ventilation.

title: Read the shape

dx.label: THE DIAGNOSIS
dx.name: Rebreathing
dx.text: Inspired gas should contain no CO2. A baseline that stays above zero means exhaled CO2 is being breathed back in.

items: **Raised inspiratory baseline:** rebreathing. Check absorbent, valves, fresh gas flow, circuit.
**Slow upstroke, sloped plateau:** expiratory obstruction.
**Notch in the plateau:** spontaneous effort (curare cleft).
**Sudden EtCO2 drop, same ventilation:** think perfusion, like embolism or low output.
! Low perfusion and high CO2 production change the waveform's height. Neither puts CO2 in inspired gas.

title: Why B

dx.label: THE DIAGNOSIS
dx.name: Anaphylaxis
dx.text: Allergen exposure, then hives, lip swelling, wheeze and hypotension within minutes.

items: **Epinephrine first.** It reverses the vasodilation, airway swelling and bronchospasm. Delay is linked to death.
**0.01 mg/kg** of 1 mg/mL epinephrine: **0.18 mg (0.18 mL)**. Max single dose 0.5 mg. Repeat every 5–15 min.
**IM, anterolateral thigh.** Faster, more reliable than subcutaneous or deltoid. Don't wait for an IV.
**Then** IV access, **20 mL/kg** crystalloid, albuterol for wheeze. Postpone the elective case.
! **D is a 10-fold overdose.** Antihistamines only help the hives. They are never first.

title: Why D

dx.label: THE PROBLEM
dx.name: A full stomach
dx.text: His labs are corrected, so he is ready for surgery. But the pylorus is blocked: secretions and barium stay in the stomach, even with an NG tube.

items: A **large multi-orifice orogastric tube** right before induction recovered an average of almost **5 mL/kg**.
Those volumes **weren't reduced** by NG suction, fasting time or a prior barium study.
Then secure the airway with **RSI or modified RSI**. Awake intubation is no longer favored.
! Prokinetics can't beat a fixed obstruction. H2 blockers don't remove fluid already there.

title: Why D

dx.label: THE DIAGNOSIS
dx.name: Renarcotization
dx.text: The naloxone wore off before the methadone did, so the respiratory depression came back.

items: Naloxone's half-life is roughly **30–80 minutes**. Methadone's is **very long**.
**Infusion, not repeat boluses.** A steady level prevents another hypoxic episode between doses.
Infuse about **two-thirds of the effective dose per hour**: 120 mcg → about 80 mcg/h.
Titrate to breathing and sedation, in a **continuously monitored** setting. Not the floor.
! Big fixed doses strip analgesia and can trigger severe pain and a catecholamine surge.
